title: Claiborne Williams band and George Williams, a Navy bandmate
summary: He praises George Williams, a first-class musician now teaching in Baton Rouge whom he saw at a parade, and mentions other Navy colleagues.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: You might tell us a little bit about the Claiborne Williams band. You were telling us outside that you were in the Navy with George Williams. With George Williams.

Very, very first class musician. And he's back in, up in Baton Rouge. He's teaching, yeah. My wife teaches school. I think he's teaching music at some school, I think. I'm not sure, but I don't know. He's also selling instruments and everything. Yeah. We played, he was standing on the corner of Jackson Avenue. The last time we played that big parade, we left him, Drys and Phillip. We had four or five bands out.

Sure. But he was standing on Jackson Avenue and, what is it, Parade? Block of Four, LaSalle. He was standing right on that corner, because I walked out the parade and went and spoke. He said, I got to leave right away, otherwise I'd follow you to talk with you, you know, because you wouldn't come to Baton Rouge and play with him. He was a very good musician. Is that this year? Oh, no, that was last year. Well, there was, there was, uh, King John.
I remember one last year that way it started. It was a Mason's parade. Yeah, right.
Prince Hall, I guess. No, it was not Prince Hall. I think it was King George. Oh, yeah, the one that had. No, St. John. St. On Phillip and Dry.
Yeah, I know, where they had the pub houses.

Yeah, but last time we left there with that big parade, he was standing on Jackson Avenue. Russ was in the Navy, Russ. Russ, Henry Russ, Said. Oh, yeah. We had a very good trombone player and music teacher from Wallace Collins and Boatron Adams.
